assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation turns a small molecule into a programmable tool that removes a target protein instead of merely inhibiting it. It opens previously undruggable targets and is a clear case of molecular design principles changing what chemists and clinicians can do; it is already spreading widely in chemical biology and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept and Crews led the first small-molecule PROTACs; Ciulli supplied the structural and mechanistic design rules (VHL ligands, ternary-complex cooperativity). Molecular glue degraders (thalidomide-cereblon, Handa, Ito, Gray) are a separate strand that would be hard to fit into three names.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials and the mechanism is well confirmed across laboratories, though approved drugs are still few. Recognition is timely but the clinical record is still being written.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be recognized together or one of them separately, given the limit of three laureates.
Exact priority among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli and the glue-degrader pioneers is uncertain and I have not verified details independently.
Clinical validation is not yet complete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow genetically encoded unnatural amino acids, giving site-specific chemistry inside living cells. It is original, conceptually clean and used widely for protein engineering, biophysical probes, bioorthogonal labeling and therapeutic proteins.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial systems; Chin extended to quadruplet codons, orthogonal ribosomes and genome recoding. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed important synthetase systems, so a three-person split leaves some credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent use across many labs; the technology is mature and stable, and recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama.
Commercial and therapeutic impact is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a major conceptual change linking physical chemistry of multivalent molecules to cell biology and disease. It strongly influences how biomaterials and condensate-like systems are thought about.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated P granules and nucleoli as liquid droplets; Rosen provided the multivalent-interaction chemistry in reconstituted systems. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-grammar theory and experiment, so credit is spread across several people.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly expanding field with extensive confirmation, but debate remains about the physiological relevance of phase separation versus other assemblies, and some claims are contested.
uncertainties: Reproducibility and in vivo relevance of some condensate claims remain debated.
Chemistry versus biology/physics classification is arguable.
Broad credit and the three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are chemistry-driven protein engineering tools that convert one base to another without double-strand breaks, directly addressing the precision limits of earlier genome editing. They have clear and fast translation into clinical therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and engineering effort; Komor and Gaudelli were first authors on the cytosine and adenine base editors, so they are the plausible co-laureates, but giving trainees a prize would be unusual. Liu alone is a defensible configuration. Nishida and Kondo reported an independent cytidine deaminase editor.
assessment.maturity: Early clinical results exist and the method is widely replicated; the long-term safety record is limited, and a Chemistry prize after the 2020 CRISPR prize may seem too close.
uncertainties: Whether recognition would be perceived as too soon after the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Whether Liu alone should be recognized and whether base and prime editing should be combined.
Long-term clinical safety is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis, built on reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule clusters, changed biology and medicine at a scale few chemical methods have achieved. Clear, lasting and transformative impact on how biomedical research and diagnostics are done.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry and platform; Mayer's colony sequencing and Rothberg's pyrosequencing platform are other strands. Credit is contested across several approaches and companies, though the Solexa pair is the most defensible chemistry core.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, decades of use, with the technology replaced and refined but the principle confirmed; it is arguably late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Dispute over credit among Solexa, Lynx, 454 and Ju's reversible terminators.
Whether it is perceived as chemistry or as a technology/biology achievement.
Facts about patent and invention order are not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the chemical enabling technology that made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable, including mRNA vaccines and siRNA therapeutics. This is an excellent example of molecular design (pKa-tuned lipids, self-assembly) translating directly into patients.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the lipid nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid development; Langer and Anderson advanced combinatorial lipidoids and delivery materials. MacLachlan, Hope and Madden are significant contributors, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Established through approved siRNA and mRNA products and strong independent confirmation; impact is evident and recognition is timely, though it follows closely the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may reduce priority.
Credit among Cullis, Langer, Anderson and others, and patent disputes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed assembly of nanoparticles and spherical nucleic acids give nanoscale building blocks with programmable recognition, and connect directly to colorimetric and plasmonic biosensing, intracellular gene regulation and diagnostics. This is design-driven molecular materials chemistry with biomedical reach.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group (with Mucic and Storhoff) and Alivisatos's group published the foundational DNA-nanoparticle assembly papers in 1996; Mirkin alone developed spherical nucleic acids. A one-to-two-laureate configuration is plausible, though Alivisatos's work could be seen as better suited to nanocrystal science.
assessment.maturity: The concept is confirmed and widely used; clinical translation of spherical nucleic acids is still limited, and diagnostic use has been modest compared with expectations.
uncertainties: Priority between Mirkin and Alivisatos in 1996.
Real-world clinical and commercial impact is moderate so far.
Alivisatos might be better recognized for nanocrystals broadly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Control of localized surface plasmon resonances in engineered nanostructures provides the basis for plasmonic sensing, photothermal therapy and light-driven catalysis. This is foundational for the nanoplasmonic biosensing I work in, though I am aware of my own bias toward this area.
assessment.attribution: Halas (nanoshells), Xia (shape-controlled synthesis) and Schatz (theory) are credible roles; Nordlander also made theoretical contributions, and El-Sayed and others are not in the supplied credit list. The distinction between synthesis, theory and application is hard to allocate.
assessment.maturity: Field is mature and widely confirmed, but the Nobel-level discovery is diffuse and overlaps with the 2023 quantum dot prize in nanomaterials, and sensing applications have had limited clinical penetration.
uncertainties: Diffuse discovery with an unclear single core contribution.
Possible overlap with the 2023 quantum dot prize.
My own field bias.
